name: layout-screen-regions
summary: Inside the content panel a standard page stacks four regions top-to-bottom: Page header (required) → Toolbar / filter bar (optional) → Body (required) → Footer / pagination (optional). The body takes one of 6 content layouts — single column, two-pane, master-detail, dashboard grid, three-pane, chart-over-grid.

toolbar.note: show the optional toolbar / filter bar

callouts.note: render the annotated 4-region wireframe instead of the interactive panel

regions: Page header — required; the page title + primary actions (carries the --primary left accent)
Toolbar / filter bar — optional; search, filters, view switches
Body — required; one of the 6 content layouts
Footer / pagination — optional; pagination, bulk-action summary
contentLayouts: three-pane — saved-views rail + picker + content (e.g. Metric Explorer)
chart-over-grid — a fixed chart above a grid (e.g. Trap Viewer / log dashboards)
do: Compose top-down: Page header → Toolbar → Body → Footer.
Mark required regions (Page header, Body) with the primary left accent.
Pick the content layout that matches the task (two-pane for tree+content, master-detail for list+record).
dont: Don't omit the Page header (it's required).
Don't use a drawer for a panel-sized record where two-pane reads better.

a11y.summary: Region grammar. The Page header hosts the page heading (h1) + primary actions; the Body is the <main> content. Required regions carry the primary left accent.

knownIssues: Shape references for the body — not live components.

[element] The obs-layout-* WEB COMPONENT is a fixed visual demo, not a slotted layout primitive — you can't put a real page inside it. Use the layout GUIDANCE (decisionFlow/regions) + compose the shell from atoms + the 12-col grid + tokens.
changelog: 2026-06-29: added — the 4-region stack + 6 content layouts; interactive shape/toolbar/footer.
2026-06-29: fixed two-pane (30/70) and three-pane (18/26/56) column proportions (were rendering as equal columns).
whenToUse: Compose a page top-to-bottom — header → (toolbar) → body → (footer) — then give the body one of six content layouts.
usedIn: Two-pane → explorers, settings · Master-detail → alert/inventory records · Dashboard grid → dashboards.
Three-pane → metric / apm explorers · Chart-over-grid → trap viewer / log dashboards.
decisionFlow: Start EVERY page with a Page header (title + primary action). Then the body picks ONE content layout:
A flat list of records? -> Single column (Toolbar/Filter bar + Table + pager).
A tree/hierarchy on the left + detail on the right? -> Two-pane (master-detail).
A list where selecting a row opens a record beside/over it? -> Master-detail (list + Drawer).
Metric tiles? -> Dashboard grid. A chart above a supporting table? -> Chart-over-grid.
Only escalate to Three-pane when a saved-views rail AND a picker are BOTH needed. Don't combine two content layouts on one screen.
